Who we are
With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility.
Co-Op- System Engineer
Term: Spring (Jan-May 2027)
At Symbotic, early career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment.

Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements.
Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity!
What we need
Symbotic is seeking a Co-Op- System Engineer to join our Site Operations team within our Customer Operations organization. Your job will be to support the performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of our robotic material handling system while developing hands-on experience across mechanical, electrical, robotics, and software technologies.
What we do
The Site Operations team leads the day-to-day operation and support of Symbotic's automated material handling systems at customer sites. The team partners closely with onsite customers and cross-functional engineering and support teams to troubleshoot issues, maintain safe operations, improve system performance, and deliver reliable automation solutions.
What you'll do
Monitor system health and help troubleshoot advanced operational, mechanical, electrical, robotics, and software-related issues.
Shadow experienced System Engineers, learn end-to-end material flow, and progressively support assigned system tickets and site activities.
Analyze system alarms, performance metrics, and operational data to identify trends, recurring issues, and improvement opportunities.
Document issues clearly, communicate technical concepts to site teams and customers, and partner with engineering and support teams on solutions.
Assist with escalations for production-impacting problems and help coordinate follow-up actions through resolution.
Own a scoped continuous improvement project that uses site data to address a recurring operational need and measure results.
Follow OSHA, Symbotic, and customer safety processes and procedures while working in an active warehouse environment.
What you'll need
Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
Foundational knowledge of robotics, automation, electromechanical systems, controls, or industrial operations.
Familiarity with one or more of the following: PLCs, SQL, Linux, Python, Power BI, Excel, data visualization, or continuous improvement practices.
Hands-on interest or experience assembling, operating, testing, or troubleshooting robotics and electromechanical equipment through coursework, projects, clubs, or prior work.
Ability to analyze data, organize findings, and translate observations into practical recommendations or actions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical information clearly to different audiences.
Curiosity, a bias for action, and willingness to ask questions, learn unfamiliar equipment, and contribute in a fast-paced customer-site environment.
Our Environment
Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ.
Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued.
This role is based onsite at a customer location and requires regular work in an active warehouse environment.
Must be able to work at heights of up to 45 feet and within restrictive areas of 24 inches.
Must be capable of working in temperatures ranging from 32 to 105 degrees Fahrenheit and standing or walking for up to 8 hours.
Frequent ability to safely and efficiently lift items weighing up to 60 pounds and move items weighing up to 80 pounds.
Must be capable of occasional or continuous feeling, seeing, hearing, bending, twisting, stooping, pushing, pulling, balancing, gripping, climbing, crawling, sitting, handling objects, and repetitive movement using both hands and feet.

Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com.

ALL ABOUT THE STORES EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP
Experience firsthand what it’s like to lead a retail team within a Target store. This internship is a paid 40 hr/week, hands-on training program to develop and prepare you for store leadership. As a Stores Executive Intern, you will get a valuable realistic preview of the Executive Team Leader role (Assistant Store Manager) over a defined period of time. Within this store management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members to develop an understanding of how Target’s retail business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. You will be introduced to multiple areas of the store’s business, but the majority of your time will be spent leading amongst the team, identifying and working towards store priorities, and delivering great guest service.
This program is designed to teach individuals how to lead within a retail store and you will:
Learn how to drive guest experience and impact your store’s financial, team, and operational performance.
Work alongside a mentor and learn how they effectively lead their department within the store.
Have the opportunity to step into leading your mentor’s departments- of course, we will be there to guide you and help you learn along the way!
Spend your days learning to lead and motivate a team, drive sales results, merchandise products, and provide an exceptional experience for our guests.
Have ongoing development conversations, as your development will be a top priority of ours.
Lead and support the execution of daily operations by working with your team members to build culture and guide your team to grow and achieve goals.
Learn more from past Interns, Mentors, and Managers here.
At Target, we believe in our leaders having meaningful experiences that help them build and develop skills for a career. The goal of the Stores Executive internship is to provide a realistic job preview of an ETL role. The role of a Stores Executive Intern can provide you with the skills and experience of:
Guest service fundamentals and experience building and managing a guest-first team culture across the store
Guest engagement; problem-solving and resolution
Retail business fundamentals
Setting and planning department(s) monthly/quarterly workload to support business priorities and managing a team to deliver service and sales goals
Managing a team of hourly team members and team leaders while creating business strategies and goals
Recruiting, selecting and talent management of hourly team members and leaders
As a Stores Executive Intern, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities:

The Walk-In Services team is the first point of contact for the nearly 2,000 new walk-in clients who visit the IRC in Silver Spring each year. We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water.
We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource.
What we do:
For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​
The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you!
Scope of Position
This motivated and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Marketing and Product Management team, will be responsible for developing technical training materials and supporting product improvement initiatives that enhance customer understanding of heat pump and water heating systems. The Heat Pump Product Engineering Intern will gain hands-on experience in technical communication, refrigeration design, and applied HVAC technology while collaborating with Product Management, Engineering, and New Product Development teams to create instructional resources, support troubleshooting activities, and evaluate potential product improvements.
This position reports to the Product Manager. This role is onsite and is based in Fort Worth, TX.
Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities
Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify common product startup challenges, troubleshooting procedures, and technical support needs.
Develop technical training materials, including instructional manuals, presentations, videos, and online training modules to support field startup and troubleshooting activities.
Research existing industry training materials and best practices to ensure instructional resources align with applicable technical standards and customer needs.
Assist with the development and organization of training content for online learning platforms to improve accessibility and usability for customers and field personnel.
Work with Product Management and Engineering teams to identify commonly failing components and evaluate potential replacement solutions.
Support product improvement initiatives by reviewing cost analysis findings, testing results, and technical recommendations.
Develop testing plans to evaluate the functionality, reliability, and durability of selected replacement components through functional and stress testing.
Collaborate with Engineering and New Product Development teams to gain an understanding of refrigeration design, heat pump systems, and applied HVAC/water heating technologies.
Assist with documenting technical findings, testing procedures, and product performance observations to support troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives.
Utilize Microsoft Office and relevant technical tools to develop training documentation, presentations, and project reports.
Participate in internship development activities, networking opportunities, and cross-functional learning experiences.
Summarize and present internship project outcomes, technical findings, and recommendations to leadership at the conclusion of the internship.
Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Training Manager, Product Manager, or Company management.
Demonstrate integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and transparency by maintaining accurate technical documentation, following established safety and testing procedures, identifying opportunities for product improvements, and effectively communicating project findings.
Required Qualifications
Current student (junior or senior status).
Pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Building Systems, HVAC Technology, Communications, or a related technical or media field.
GPA of 3.0 or higher.
Strong interest in technical training, renewable energy, and/or HVAC and water heating systems.
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to participate in hands-on demonstrations and technical activities under supervision.
Demonstrated initiative, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail.
Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact.
Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment.
Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments.
Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable.
Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.
Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks and required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment.
Preferred Qualifications
Completion of junior- or senior-level coursework in a relevant field.
Familiarity with computer-aided design (CAD), diagramming, or graphic design tools such as SolidWorks, AutoCAD, Visio, or Adobe Illustrator.
Interest in technical documentation, instructional content development, or product training.
Interest in refrigeration systems, heat pump technology, or HVAC equipment.
General Applicable Company Competencies
Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency.
Punctuality and dependability.
Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions.
Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts.
Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees.
Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action.
Working Conditions
While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at the Fort Worth, TX location in both an office and manufacturing environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager.
Physical Requirements: Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to:
Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods.
Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials.
Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks.
Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls.
Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers.
Ability to stand for long periods of time.
Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds.
Ability to push and pull up to 25 pounds.
Ability to physically move around manufacturing floor.
Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers.
Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses.
Pay Range: $22-26
The expected hourly range for this position is $22–$26 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law.
What's In It for You
People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected.
Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence.
Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday.
Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model!
Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen.
Nothing in this job description restricts Watts’ right to assign or reassign duties, responsibilities, and working hours/conditions to this position at any time. This position is “at will,” which means that either the employee or Watts may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, and for any lawful reason.

Continued professional development opportunities and educational reimbursement
Additional perks such as fitness reimbursements and employee discount programs

At Watts, our culture is team-oriented and supportive. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success.

About the team
The forecasting and business economics group at Zillow shapes planning and drives decision making across Zillow’s businesses. Embedded in the finance organization, our team prioritizes research projects that directly impact the company’s bottom line and growth.
We bring together forecasters, economists, applied scientists, data scientists, and data visualization engineers to build forecasts and craft research that elevates how our businesses operate. We transform our industry-leading data with our expertise in statistics and economics into actionable insights that inform decisions at every level of the company. Our work combines state of the art quantitative methods across forecasting, data science, and causal inference to help answer practical questions for our business leaders.
About the role
At Zillow, interns do meaningful work that contributes to the business from day one. Our 9 week summer internship program, running June 14th through August 13th, gives students the opportunity to bring their ideas and perspectives to real projects alongside Zillow teams.
Interns build hands-on experience, connect with mentors and leaders, and take part in learning and community experiences with their intern cohort. Our 2027 internships are based in Seattle and follow a hybrid schedule, with interns generally working together in person Tuesday through Thursday. Eligible interns will receive a stipend to help offset summer housing and relocation costs.
We’re looking for students who are analytical and detail-oriented with the ability to create structure from ambiguity. You have an intense curiosity to learn and can do so in a fast-paced dynamic environment. If you are not afraid of working with large amounts of data, you’ll get the chance to make it all come together into meaningful metrics used to make strategic business decisions.
During your internship, you will have opportunities to:
Partner with your manager and stakeholders to translate open-ended business questions into an analytical approach, with clear deliverables that will directly translate to tangible benefits to revenue.
Explore, clean, and validate housing, economic, business, or financial data; document assumptions and identify data-quality issues.
Build and compare models to support prediction and forecasting.
Transform observational data into causal models using clever identification
Design experiments to improve how we price and operate across our different businesses
Evaluate models using appropriate baselines and time-based validation, and communicate uncertainty, limitations, and trade-offs.
Investigate trends, forecast errors, and drivers of business performance to develop actionable insights.
Create reproducible analyses, visualizations, or reporting workflows that help partners understand and use your findings.
Share your approach, results, and recommendations with technical and nontechnical audiences, and document your work for a clear handoff.
This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.
In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $104,000.00 - $166,000.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.
Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location.
Who you are
Currently pursuing a Masters or PhD in statistics, economics, data science, applied mathematics, quantitative finance, or a related quantitative field, with an expected graduation between December 2027 and Summer 2028.
Strong foundation in probability, statistics, and regression analysis, with exposure to econometrics. Specifically time-series and causal analysis through coursework and research experience.
Use AI tools to accelerate and expand their work without outsourcing their own thinking to it.
Can use Python or similar to prepare data, conduct analysis, and build models. Even if you’re not writing code anymore, we expect an ability to express statistical concepts clearly through pseudocode and think through edgecases when designing systems.
Can explain analytical findings clearly and collaborate with people who bring different perspectives and expertise including non technical stakeholders.
Move quickly and ambitiously without sacrificing attention to detail; enjoy zooming in and out based on context.
Approach problems thoughtfully: you check your assumptions, validate results, and distinguish what the data supports from what remains uncertain.
Are interested in applying quantitative methods to housing markets, business forecasting, and financial decision-making.
Get to know us
At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.
How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.
Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.
No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.
